findings.description: The `initial` attribute was replaced by `multiplier`, so any code reading `wait.initial` now breaks. In addition, `initial` is compared against the default 1 rather than a sentinel, so an explicit `initial=1` cannot be told apart from the default.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `wait_exponential_jitter(initial=1, multiplier=5)`. Both guards (`initial != 1`) are false, so the call succeeds with multiplier=5 and no error or deprecation warning, although both were given. The constructor also no longer sets `self.initial`, so subclasses or user code that read `.initial` raise AttributeError.
